title: 1983 AHSME Problem 20
statement: If \(\tan\alpha\) and \(\tan\beta\) are the roots of \(x^2-px+q=0,\) and \(\cot\alpha\) and \(\cot\beta\) are the roots of \(x^2-rx+s=0,\) then \(rs\) is necessarily

solutions.text:
Let the first roots be \(u=\tan\alpha\) and \(v=\tan\beta.\) Then \(u+v=p\) and \(uv=q.\) The second roots are \(\frac{1}{u}\) and \(\frac{1}{v},\) so \[ \begin{aligned} r&=\frac1u+\frac1v=\frac pq,\\ s&=\frac1{uv}=\frac1q. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \(rs=\frac{p}{q^2}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.

Use Vieta’s formulas to express their sum and product in terms of \(p,q\)
